verdict.rationale: Sentry's docs show an Issues page for seeing and debugging application errors, stack traces surfaced with suspect commits, and release management through the CLI with deploy notifications. Regression detection is not evidenced at all, and the docs never explicitly describe how errors are grouped into issues. missing for 10: regression detection evidence, explicit documentation of error grouping/fingerprinting into issues, depth on release tracking (release health/association of errors to releases), independent hands-on corroboration

support.subject: As a developer, I can see application errors grouped into issues with stack traces, release tracking, and regression detection

citations.quote: Learn how to use Sentry's Issues page, where you can see and start to debug errors and performance problems that are affecting your application.
Suspect commits, stack traces, and PR comments.
It’s primarily used for managing debug information files for iOS, Android, release and source maps management
Deploy notifications and source map uploads.
This page allows you to filter by properties such as browser, device, impacted users, or whether an error is unhandled.
